openChangeRequests.ask: WorkspaceInstance has no instance-level brief, and no favorite / lastOpenedAt.
openChangeRequests.why: The Brief surface is one of four mandated workspace surfaces and currently has nothing authoritative to render. WorkspaceBlueprint.description describes the template, so every workspace from one blueprint would show identical text.
openChangeRequests.loop02Workaround: WorkspaceView.brief is optional and the Brief surface renders an explicit 'not set' affordance rather than borrowing blueprint text. favorite is held as local UI state in the shell and declared as a device preference, not domain truth.

openChangeRequests.ask: ApprovalActionBinding.input is typed unknown, so the shell has no safe way to render an action preview.
openChangeRequests.why: An operator approving an external effect should see what will be sent. The doc comment promises redaction but the type cannot enforce it, and blind-rendering an unknown risks putting a raw payload or secret-shaped value on a primary surface.
openChangeRequests.loop02Workaround: binding.input is NEVER rendered. The preview shows binding.target and binding.estimatedSideEffect only. Proposal on record: producer-supplied, pre-redacted previewFields.

openChangeRequests.ask: Approval carries no post-decision outcome, and no link from an approved Approval to the resulting Artifact or follow-up event.
openChangeRequests.why: 'Receive the deliverable' is the last step of the primary workflow. Without an outcome the operator approves into a void and the shell cannot render an honest receipt.
openChangeRequests.loop02Workaround: No receipt is faked. The approval card exposes no outcome claim at all.

openChangeRequests.ask: Expose a create-run intent, e.g. CreateRunIntent { goal, workspaceInstanceId }.
openChangeRequests.why: WorkRun requires rootRunId, lineageKind, attempt, planVersion, planHash and appliedEventSequence. A renderer cannot supply any of them, and must not invent them.
openChangeRequests.loop02Workaround: WorkDataSource.delegate takes { goal, workspaceId } and the engine assembles the run. The shell never constructs a WorkRun literal.

openChangeRequests.ask: No workspace bootstrap path is specified: WorkRun.workspaceInstanceId is required and WorkspaceInstance.blueprintId is required, so a first-run operator with no blueprint and no workspace cannot delegate at all.
openChangeRequests.why: This directly threatens the acceptance criterion 'launch to delegating a sample brief in at most two actions'.
openChangeRequests.loop02Workaround: The shell does NOT synthesize a workspace. With no data it shows an honest empty state and the composer is disabled with a stated reason. The quarantine draft's fabricated REAL_WORKSPACE_ID = 'personal' was deleted.

securityGate.residualRisk: WorkRun.goal is operator-authored free text and is rendered at L1 by necessity, so a primary surface can contain whatever the operator typed, including customer names. This is inherent, not a defect. Mitigation is screenshot hygiene: capture only demo fixtures. Secondly, redaction is defence in depth on top of a producer promise the type system cannot enforce; if an upstream field embeds a secret in prose the regexes are heuristic, not proof.

outputs: Five top-level routes and no more: Today (default landing), Workspaces, MyGraph, Market, Settings.

Exactly four workspace surfaces: Brief, Work, Deliverables, Approvals. Context, Apps, Brand, Knowledge, Agents/Skills, Policies and Runtime live in a setup drawer and are structurally incapable of becoming tabs.
Today renders three lanes off RunState with waiting_external in 'Waiting for me', plus a separate always-visible attention band so a failed run is never invisible.
Delegate composer on the landing route, so launch to delegated brief is two actions: type the goal, press Delegate.
Command palette on Ctrl/Cmd+K and '/' with an explicit focus trap, arrow/Home/End navigation, aria-activedescendant, and focus restored to the prior element on close.
Six presentation states resolved by one precedence function: loading > error > offline > degraded > empty > ready.
One adapter seam: WorkDataSource. W3 changes exactly one function, resolveDataSource(), and no component or view model moves.
Feature flag izzi.shell.personalOffice with in-place rollback to the untouched legacy sidebar shell, reachable from Settings, with no reload and no lost session.

Legacy catalogue of 18 surfaces: nothing deleted, nothing re-implemented. AI Marketing and Phong Marketing are catalogued inside one Marketing group instead of being flat peers, and task/agent/model are no longer primary navigation.
MyGraph is a route shell only; Loop 04 owns the graph internals and no graph styling was touched.
docs/product/personal-office-ia.md records the route map, component map, legacy catalogue, flag and rollback behaviour, and the responsive, accessibility and state matrices.

skillAudit.effect: Searched for existing shell, nav, store and icon patterns before writing anything. Found and reused components/AppIcons.tsx (only 10 genuinely missing glyphs were added), the existing :root token block, and the per-page CSS import convention. Also established by search that docs/product/, producer-environment.json and Playwright genuinely did not exist rather than assuming either way.

Assembled the gate state each turn: worktree, branch, HEAD, ancestry, lease terms, acceptance record, salvage conditions. This is what caught that Loop 01 was unaccepted in earlier turns, that my own 663de47 commit message overstated the mount, and that the earlier evidence directory contained no screenshots.

Mapped App.tsx's useState<Page> routing, the navigationMap.test.ts text contract, the agentWorkspace store shape and the token system. Directly determined the mount design: an added early return plus a defaulted renderPage parameter, which keeps the asserted text contract byte-identical.

Drove component boundaries, tab semantics with roving tabindex, the focus trap and focus restore in the palette, sheet and drawer, live-region politeness levels, the single state-precedence resolver, and deriving run progress from steps rather than denormalising it.

Produced the securityGate block. Concretely changed the code: toSafeMessage and toFileLabel exist because of it, binding.input is never rendered, hashes are L3-only, demo defaults to off so an empty install cannot show fabricated work, and unwired approve buttons do not render at all.

Ran typecheck, full tests, lint:ci, build, diff --check, ownership audit and secret scan; all pass. It also caught the one new lint warning, which I removed rather than raising the ceiling. Partial because the UI and accessibility half could not run without the PQ-01 lease; that is recorded as unmet, not as passing.

Set the calm-professional cockpit direction and the anti-slop constraints actually honoured in the CSS: no gradient fills on shell surfaces, no hero, no decorative blobs, no card-inside-card, restrained token subset, hairline borders, tabular numerals for counts.
Kept every value token-driven against the existing :root block rather than introducing a parallel palette, and added no new :root override block.

skillAudit.reason: Landing-page and portfolio oriented: AIDA structure, hero sections, scroll hijacking and GSAP scroll-triggers. Applying any of it to a dense single-operator desktop cockpit would actively damage the product. Read for anti-slop cues only, not applied.
Same landing and portfolio bias. Its audit-first instinct informed reading the existing token system before styling, but its page-structure prescriptions do not apply to an app shell.
No server, API or data-layer work. The adapter is a read-only projection over contract types and adds no IPC, no persistence and no endpoint. main/** was prohibited.
No CI, CD, container or rollout work in this loop. Rollback here is a client-side feature flag, not a deployment strategy, and no deploy or publish was performed.
